fullText.simplified:
孟姜女哭倒长城

    长城大家都知道。今天我们看到的长城，宏伟壮观。然而，这宏伟的长城背后，凝结了无数古代劳动人民的心血和汗水。今天，我们要讲的就是一个与长城有关的凄美的爱情故事。
    秦朝时候，有个善良美丽的女子，名叫孟姜女。
    一天，她正在自家院子里做家务，突然发现葡萄架下藏着一个人。孟姜女吓了一大跳，正想叫人。只见那个人连连摆手，哀求道：“小姐，拜托你千万别喊。我无意冒犯。我叫范喜良，是逃难来到这里的，快救救我吧！”原来，那个时候，秦始皇为了盖长城，正在到处抓人做劳工，已经饿死、累死了不知多少人。很多人为了不被抓去做劳工，都背井离乡，躲避官兵的追赶。
    孟姜女听了范喜良的遭遇后，把范喜良救了下来，并让他住在家里。日久生情，他们俩人相爱了。孟姜女的父母也很喜欢范喜良，便同意了他们的婚事。
    成亲那天，孟家张灯结彩，宾客满堂，一派喜气洋洋的情景。眼看天快黑了，喝喜酒的宾客也都渐渐散了。新郎新娘正要进洞房，忽然听到门外鸡飞狗跳，随后闯进来了一大群官兵。他们不由分说，硬把范喜良抓去为秦始皇盖长城了。
    好端端的喜事变成了一场空，孟姜女悲愤交加，日夜思念着丈夫。她每天都盼着丈夫回来，但人没盼回来，连信都没有一封回来。实在放心不下的孟姜女，决定亲自去长城寻找丈夫。
    长城离她家很远很远。一路上，孟姜女不知经历了多少风霜雨雪，跋涉过多少险山恶水。但孟姜女没喊过一声苦，也没掉过一滴泪。终于，她凭着顽强的毅力和对丈夫深深的爱，到达了长城。
    这时的长城，已经是由一个个工地组成的一道很长很长的城墙了。孟姜女一个工地一个工地地找过来，却始终不见丈夫的踪影。她鼓起勇气，问了一队正要上工的工人：“你们这儿有个叫范喜良的人吗？”
    工人们说：“有这么一个人，新来不久的。”
    孟姜女一听，别提有多高兴了。她接着问：“那他人呢？”
    工人们你看看我，我看看你，过了很久才说：“范喜良……上个月的时候，因为疲劳和饥饿，已经死了。”
    孟姜女又问：“那他的尸首呢？”
    工人们摇摇头说：“唉，死的人太多了，根本埋不过来。上面的吩咐我们把他填到长城里了。”
    突然听到这个噩耗，孟姜女只觉得晴天霹雳，她拍着长城，大哭了起来。她整整哭了三天三夜，哭得天昏地暗，连天地都感动了。突然，在她的哭声中，一声“哗啦啦”的巨响，长城竟像天崩地裂一样倒塌了一大段，成堆的人骨露了出来。可是那么多的白骨，哪一个才是自己的丈夫呢？很快她就通过自己亲手为丈夫做的衣服，认出了丈夫的尸骨。孟姜女守着丈夫的尸骨，哭得死去活来。
    正在她哭着的时候，秦始皇带领大队人马，从这里路过。他听说孟姜女把长城哭倒了，气得火冒三丈。他带领大队人马来到山下，准备处置孟姜女。但是，当他看到孟姜女是一个那么年轻貌美的姑娘时，立即改变了主意，产生了霸占她的想法。
    秦始皇想娶孟姜女为妻，孟姜女说：“你要答应我三件事，我就嫁给你。”
    秦始皇很高兴，笑眯眯地说：“不要说三件事，就是三十件事，我也依你。说吧，你要什么？”
    孟姜女说：“第一件，我要你给我丈夫立碑、修坟；第二件，我要你给我丈夫披麻戴孝；第三件，我要你陪我逛三天大海。”
    秦始皇答应了。
    在做完第二件事后，孟姜女说：“走吧，我们去游海吧！”
    秦始皇喜出望外，以为他游完海后就可以和孟姜女成亲了。谁知，正当他高兴的时候，只听“扑通”一声，孟姜女跳进了大海，再也找不到了。
    孟姜女哭倒长城的故事，在我国广为流传，可以说是家喻户晓。它是中国民间四大爱情故事之一。后人为了纪念她，在山海关附近的一个山头上，为她修坟建庙，并取名为“姜女庙”。

sentences.traditional: 連信都沒有一封回來。
sentences.pinyin: lián xìn dōu méi yǒu yì fēng huí lái
sentences.english: Every day, she would hope for her husband’s return, but he did not come back as she had hoped.

sentences.simplified: 实在放心不下的孟姜女，决定亲自去长城寻找丈夫。
sentences.traditional: 實在放心不下的孟姜女，決定親自去長城尋找丈夫。
sentences.pinyin: shí zài fàng xīn bú xià de mèng jiāng nǚ jué dìng qīn zì qù cháng chéng xún zhǎo zhàng fu
sentences.english: Not even a single letter came.
Lady Meng Jiang was really worried and decided to go personally to the Great Wall to look for her husband.

sentences.simplified: 长城离她家很远很远。
sentences.traditional: 長城離她家很遠很遠。
sentences.pinyin: cháng chéng lí tā jiā hěn yuǎn hěn yuǎn

sentences.simplified: 一路上，孟姜女不知经历了多少风霜雨雪，
sentences.traditional: 一路上，孟姜女不知經歷了多少風霜雨雪，
sentences.pinyin: yí lù shang mèng jiāng nǚ bù zhī jīng lì le duō shao fēng shuāng yǔ xuě
sentences.english: The Great Wall was very, very far from her home.

sentences.simplified: 跋涉过多少险山恶水。
sentences.traditional: 跋涉過多少險山惡水。
sentences.pinyin: bá shè guò duō shao xiǎn shān ě shuǐ
sentences.english: Along the way, Lady Meng Jiang experienced countless bouts of wind, frost, rain, and snow.

sentences.simplified: 但孟姜女没喊过一声苦，也没掉过一滴泪。
sentences.traditional: 但孟姜女沒喊過一聲苦，也沒掉過一滴淚。
sentences.pinyin: dàn mèng jiāng nǚ méi hǎn guò yì shēng kǔ yě méi diào guò yì dī lèi
sentences.english: She trekked through countless dangerous mountains and treacherous waters.

sentences.simplified: 终于，她凭着顽强的毅力和对丈夫深深的爱，到达了长城。
sentences.traditional: 終於，她憑著頑強的毅力和對丈夫深深的愛，到達了長城。
sentences.pinyin: zhōng yú tā píng zhe wán qiáng de yì lì hé duì zhàng fu shēn shēn de ài dào dá le cháng chéng
sentences.english: But Lady Meng Jiang didn’t once cry out in suffering, nor did she shed a single tear.
Finally, through her tenacious willpower and deep love for her husband, she arrived at the Great Wall.

sentences.simplified: 这时的长城，已经是由一个个工地组成的一道很长很长的城墙了。
sentences.traditional: 這時的長城，已經是由一個個工地組成的一道很長很長的城牆了。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí de cháng chéng yǐ jīng shì yóu yí gè gè gōng dì zǔ chéng de yí dào hěn cháng hěn cháng de chéng qiáng le

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女一个工地一个工地地找过来，却始终不见丈夫的踪影。
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女一個工地一個工地地找過來，卻始終不見丈夫的蹤影。
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ yí ge gōng dì yí ge gōng dì de zhǎo guò lái què shǐ zhōng bú jiàn zhàng fu de zōng yǐng
sentences.english: At the time, the Great Wall had already become a very long city wall made up of individual construction sites.

sentences.simplified: 她鼓起勇气，问了一队正要上工的工人：
sentences.traditional: 她鼓起勇氣，問了一隊正要上工的工人：
sentences.pinyin: tā gǔ qǐ yǒng qì wèn le yí duì zhèng yào shàng gōng de gōng rén
sentences.english: Lady Meng Jiang searched each construction site, but didn’t find any trace of her husband.

sentences.simplified: “你们这儿有个叫范喜良的人吗？”
sentences.traditional: “你們這兒有個叫范喜良的人嗎？”
sentences.pinyin: nǐ men zhè‘r yǒu ge jiào fàn xǐ liáng de rén ma
sentences.english: She summoned the courage to ask a group of workers who were just starting work:
“Is there a person called Fan Xiliang around here?”

sentences.simplified: 工人们说：“有这么一个人，新来不久的。”
sentences.traditional: 工人們說：“有這麼一個人，新來不久的。”
sentences.pinyin: gōng rén men shuō yǒu zhè me yí ge rén xīn lái bù jiǔ de

sentences.english: The workers said: “There is such a person, he’s new and came not too long ago.”

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女一听，别提有多高兴了。
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女一聽，別提有多高興了。
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ yì tīng bié tí yǒu duō gāo xìng le

sentences.simplified: 她接着问：“那他人呢？”
sentences.traditional: 她接著問：“那他人呢？”
sentences.pinyin: tā jiē zhe wèn nà tā rén ne
sentences.english: As soon as Lady Meng Jiang heard this, she was indescribably happy.
She continued to ask: “Then where is he?”

sentences.simplified: 工人们你看看我，我看看你，过了很久才说：
sentences.traditional: 工人們你看看我，我看看你，過了很久才說：
sentences.pinyin: gōng rén men nǐ kàn kan wǒ wǒ kàn kan nǐ guò le hěn jiǔ cái shuō

sentences.simplified: “范喜良……上个月的时候，因为疲劳和饥饿，已经死了。”
sentences.traditional: “范喜良……上個月的時候，因為疲勞和飢餓，已經死了。”
sentences.pinyin: fàn xǐ liáng shàng ge yuè de shí hou yīn wèi pí láo hé jī è yǐ jīng sǐ le
sentences.english: The workers looked at each other, and after a long time finally said:
“Fan Xiliang … died last month due to exhaustion and starvation.”

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女又问：“那他的尸首呢？”
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女又問：“那他的屍首呢？”
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ yòu wèn nà tā de shī shou ne

sentences.english: Lady Meng Jiang once again asked: “Then where is his body?”

sentences.simplified: 工人们摇摇头说：
sentences.traditional: 工人們搖搖頭說：
sentences.pinyin: gōng rén men yáo yáo tóu shuō

sentences.simplified: “唉，死的人太多了，根本埋不过来。上面的吩咐我们把他填到长城里了。”
sentences.traditional: “唉，死的人太多了，根本埋不過來。上面的吩咐我們把他填到長城裡了。”
sentences.pinyin: ài sǐ de rén tài duō le gēn běn mái bú guò lái shàng miàn de fēn fù wǒ men bǎ tā tián dào cháng chéng lǐ le
sentences.english: The workers shook their heads and said:
“Alas, too many people have died, we are unable to bury them. Those above told us to fill him into the Great Wall.

sentences.simplified: 突然听到这个噩耗，孟姜女只觉得晴天霹雳，她拍着长城，大哭了起来。
sentences.traditional: 突然聽到這個噩耗，孟姜女只覺得晴天霹靂，她拍著長城，大哭了起來。
sentences.pinyin: tū rán tīng dào zhè ge è hào mèng jiāng nǚ zhǐ jué de qíng tiān pī lì tā pāi zhe cháng chéng dà kū le qǐ lái

sentences.simplified: 她整整哭了三天三夜，哭得天昏地暗，连天地都感动了。
sentences.traditional: 她整整哭了三天三夜，哭得天昏地暗，連天地都感動了。
sentences.pinyin: tā zhěng zhěng kū le sān tiān sān yè kū de tiān hūn dì àn lián tiān dì dōu gǎn dòng le
sentences.english: Suddenly hearing this grievous news was a bolt from the blue for Lady Meng Jiang. She beat the Great Wall and began to cry loudly.

sentences.simplified: 突然，在她的哭声中，一声“哗啦啦”的巨响，
sentences.traditional: 突然，在她的哭聲中，一聲“嘩啦啦”的巨響，
sentences.pinyin: tū rán zài tā de kū shēng zhōng yì shēng huā lā lā de jù xiǎng
sentences.english: She cried for three full days and three nights. She cried until it was dark all around. Even the heavens and earth were moved.

sentences.simplified: 长城竟像天崩地裂一样倒塌了一大段，成堆的人骨露了出来。
sentences.traditional: 長城竟像天崩地裂一樣倒塌了一大段，成堆的人骨露了出來。
sentences.pinyin: cháng chéng jìng xiàng tiān bēng dì liè yí yàng dǎo tā le yí dà duàn chéng duī de rén gǔ lòu le chū lái
sentences.english: Suddenly, amidst the sound of her weeping, there was a big crashing sound.

sentences.simplified: 可是那么多的白骨，哪一个才是自己的丈夫呢？
sentences.traditional: 可是那麼多的白骨，哪一個才是自己的丈夫呢？
sentences.pinyin: kě shì nà me duō de bái gǔ nǎ yí ge cái shì zì jǐ de zhàng fu ne
sentences.english: One large section of the Great Wall actually collapsed as if rocked by a major disaster. Piles of human bones were exposed.

sentences.simplified: 很快她就通过自己亲手为丈夫做的衣服，认出了丈夫的尸骨。
sentences.traditional: 很快她就通過自己親手為丈夫做的衣服，認出了丈夫的屍骨。
sentences.pinyin: hěn kuài tā jiù tōng guò zì jǐ qīn shǒu wèi zhàng fu zuò de yī fu rèn chū le zhàng fu de shī gǔ
sentences.english: But there were so many bones of the dead, which ones belonged to her husband?

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女守着丈夫的尸骨，哭得死去活来。
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女守著丈夫的屍骨，哭得死去活來。
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ shǒu zhe zhàng fu de shī gǔ kū de sǐ qù huó lái
sentences.english: Very quickly she recognized her husband’s corpse from the clothing she had made for him with her own hands.
Lady Meng Jiang guarded her husband’s corpose, and cried as though she was hovering between life and death.

sentences.simplified: 正在她哭着的时候，秦始皇带领大队人马，从这里路过。
sentences.traditional: 正在她哭著的時候，秦始皇帶領大隊人馬，從這裡路過。
sentences.pinyin: zhèng zài tā kū zhe de shí hou qín shǐ huáng dài lǐng dà duì rén mǎ cóng zhè lǐ lù guò

sentences.simplified: 他听说孟姜女把长城哭倒了，气得火冒三丈。
sentences.traditional: 他聽說孟姜女把長城哭倒了，氣得火冒三丈。
sentences.pinyin: tā tīng shuō mèng jiāng nǚ bǎ cháng chéng kū dǎo le qì de huǒ mào sān zhàng
sentences.english: Just as she was crying, Qin Shihuang led a large squadron of men and horses to pass through the area.

sentences.simplified: 他带领大队人马来到山下，准备处置孟姜女。
sentences.traditional: 他帶領大隊人馬來到山下，準備處置孟姜女。
sentences.pinyin: tā dài lǐng dà duì rén mǎ lái dào shān xià zhǔn bèi chǔ zhì mèng jiāng nǚ
sentences.english: He had heard that Lady Meng Jiang collapsed the Great Wall with her crying, and got really angry.

sentences.simplified: 但是，当他看到孟姜女是一个那么年轻貌美的姑娘时，立即改变了主意，产生了霸占她的想法。
sentences.traditional: 但是，當他看到孟姜女是一個那麼年輕貌美的姑娘時，立即改變了主意，產生了霸佔她的想法。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì dāng tā kàn dào mèng jiāng nǚ shì yí ge nà me nián qīng mào měi de gū niang shí lì jí gǎi biàn le zhǔ yi chǎn shēng le bà zhàn tā de xiǎng fǎ
sentences.english: He led the large squadron of men and horses to the bottom of the mountain, preparing to punish Lady Meng Jiang.
However, when he saw what a young and beautiful girl Lady Meng Jiang was, he immediately changed his mind, and had the idea to capture her.

sentences.simplified: 秦始皇想娶孟姜女为妻，孟姜女说：
sentences.traditional: 秦始皇想娶孟姜女為妻，孟姜女說：
sentences.pinyin: qín shǐ huáng xiǎng qǔ mèng jiāng nǚ wéi qī mèng jiāng nǚ shuō

sentences.simplified: “你要答应我三件事，我就嫁给你。”
sentences.traditional: “你要答應我三件事，我就嫁給你。”
sentences.pinyin: nǐ yào dā ying wǒ sān jiàn shì wǒ jiù jià gěi nǐ
sentences.english: Qin Shihuang wanted to take Lady Meng Jiang to be his wife. Lady Meng Jiang said:
“If you agree to three conditions, I will marry you.”

sentences.simplified: 秦始皇很高兴，笑眯眯地说：
sentences.traditional: 秦始皇很高興，笑眯眯地說：
sentences.pinyin: qín shǐ huáng hěn gāo xìng xiào mī mī de shuō

sentences.simplified: “不要说三件事，就是三十件事，我也依你。说吧，你要什么？”
sentences.traditional: “不要說三件事，就是三十件事，我也依你。說吧，你要什麼？”
sentences.pinyin: bú yào shuō sān jiàn shì jiù shì sān shí jiàn shì wǒ yě yī nǐ shuō ba nǐ yào shén me
sentences.english: Qin Shihuang was very happy, and said beamingly:
“Don’t mention three conditions, even if you ask for thirty conditions, I will do as you say. Speak, what do you want?”

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女说：
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女說：
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ shuō

sentences.simplified: “第一件，我要你给我丈夫立碑、修坟；
sentences.traditional: “第一件，我要你給我丈夫立碑、修墳；
sentences.pinyin: dì yī jiàn wǒ yào nǐ gěi wǒ zhàng fu lì bēi xiū fén
sentences.english: Lady Meng Jiang said:

sentences.simplified: 第二件，我要你给我丈夫披麻戴孝；
sentences.traditional: 第二件，我要你給我丈夫披麻戴孝；
sentences.pinyin: dì èr jiàn wǒ yào nǐ gěi wǒ zhàng fu pī má dài xiào
sentences.english: “The first condition is, I want you to erect a headstone and decorate a tomb for my husband.

sentences.simplified: 第三件，我要你陪我逛三天大海。”
sentences.traditional: 第三件，我要你陪我逛三天大海。”
sentences.pinyin: dì sān jiàn wǒ yào nǐ péi wǒ guàng sān tiān dà hǎi
sentences.english: The second condition is, I want you to dress in mourning clothes for my husband.
The third condition is, I want you to accompany me to visit the ocean for three days.”

sentences.simplified: 秦始皇答应了。
sentences.traditional: 秦始皇答應了。
sentences.pinyin: qín shǐ huáng dā ying le

sentences.english: Qin Shihuang agreed.

sentences.simplified: 在做完第二件事后，孟姜女说：“走吧，我们去游海吧！”
sentences.traditional: 在做完第二件事後，孟姜女說：“走吧，我們去遊海吧！”
sentences.pinyin: zài zuò wán dì èr jiàn shì hòu mèng jiāng nǚ shuō zǒu ba wǒ men qù yóu hǎi ba

sentences.english: After the second condition was met, Lady Meng Jiang said: “Let’s go! Let’s go to the ocean!”

sentences.simplified: 秦始皇喜出望外，以为他游完海后就可以和孟姜女成亲了。
sentences.traditional: 秦始皇喜出望外，以為他遊完海後就可以和孟姜女成親了。
sentences.pinyin: qín shǐ huáng xǐ chū wàng wài yǐ wéi tā yóu wán hǎi hòu jiù kě yǐ hé mèng jiāng nǚ chéng qīn le

sentences.simplified: 谁知，正当他高兴的时候，只听“扑通”一声，
sentences.traditional: 誰知，正當他高興的時候，只聽“撲通”一聲，
sentences.pinyin: shéi zhī zhèng dāng tā gāo xìng de shí hou zhǐ tīng pū tōng yì shēng
sentences.english: Qin Shihuang was pleased beyond his expectations, thinking that after going to the ocean he could get married to Lady Meng Jiang.

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女跳进了大海，再也找不到了。
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女跳進了大海，再也找不到了。
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ tiào jìn le dà hǎi zài yě zhǎo bú dào le
sentences.english: Who would’ve known that just as he was feeling overjoyed, he would hear a “plop” sound.
Lady Meng Jiang had jumped into the ocean, and was never to be found again.

sentences.simplified: 孟姜女哭倒长城的故事，在我国广为流传，
sentences.traditional: 孟姜女哭倒長城的故事，在我國廣為流傳，
sentences.pinyin: mèng jiāng nǚ kū dǎo cháng chéng de gù shi zài wǒ guó guǎng wéi liú chuán

sentences.simplified: 可以说是家喻户晓。它是中国民间四大爱情故事之一。
sentences.traditional: 可以說是家喻戶曉。它是中國民間四大愛情故事之一。
sentences.pinyin: kě yǐ shuō shì jiā yù hù xiǎo tā shì zhōng guó mín jiān sì dà ài qíng gù shi zhī yī
sentences.english: The story of Lady Meng Jiang collapsing the Great Wall with her crying has spread far and wide in China.

sentences.simplified: 后人为了纪念她，在山海关附近的一个山头上，为她修坟建庙，
sentences.traditional: 後人為了紀念她，在山海關附近的一個山頭上，為她修墳建廟，
sentences.pinyin: hòu rén wèi le jì niàn tā zài shān hǎi guān fù jìn de yí ge shān tóu shang wèi tā xiū fén jiàn miào
sentences.english: We can say that it is known by everyone. It is one of China’s Four Great Folktales.

sentences.simplified: 并取名为“姜女庙”。
sentences.traditional: 並取名為“姜女廟”。
sentences.pinyin: bìng qǔ míng wéi jiāng nǚ miào
sentences.english: In order to commemorate her, later generations decorated a grave and built a temple for her atop a mountain near the Shanhai Pass.
They named it the “Meng Jiangnu Temple”.

sentence_translations: Lady Meng Jiang collapses the Great Wall with her tears
Everyone knows the Great Wall.
Today the Great Wall that we all see is grand and magnificent.
However, behind the grandeur of this Great Wall lies the painstaking effort and sweat of countless laborers of ancient times.
Today, we are going to talk about a poignant love story related to the Great Wall.
In the Qin Dynasty, there was a kindhearted and beautiful girl. Her name was Lady Meng Jiang.
One day, when she was doing housework in her family’s yard, she suddenly discovered a person hiding behind the grape trellis.
Lady Meng Jiang jumped right out of her skin, and was just about to call for someone.
But she saw the person repeatedly waving their hands, pleading,
“Miss, please, by all means, don’t shout. I didn’t mean to offend.
My name is Fan Xiliang, I ran away from trouble to get here. Quick, save me!”
As it turns out, at that time, Qin Shihuang, in order to build the Great Wall, was rounding up people for physical labor.
Countless people had already starved or exhausted to death.
In order to avoid being captured to do physical labor, many people left their native place, evading the pursuit of officers and men.
After Lady Meng Jiang heard about Fan Xiliang’s misfortunes, she rescued him, and even allowed him to live in her home.
Familiarity breeds fondness, and the two of them fell in love.
Lady Meng Jiang’s parents also really liked Fan Xiliang, and approved of their marriage.
On the day they were to get married, the Meng’s home was decorated with lanterns and colored banners, and was full of guests.
It was a scene of jubilation.
Soon, the sky quickly grew dark, and the guests who attended the wedding feast were also gradually dispersing.
Just as the bride and groom were to enter the bridal room, all of a sudden they heard a great commotion outside the door.
Soon after, a large group of officers and men charged in.
They allowed no explanation, and forcedly rounded up Fan Xiliang to build the Great Wall for Qin Shihuang.
A perfect wedding came to nothing.
Lady Meng Jiang was in grief and indignation, and she thought of her husband day and night.
Every day, she would hope for her husband’s return, but he did not come back as she had hoped.
Not even a single letter came.
Lady Meng Jiang was really worried and decided to go personally to the Great Wall to look for her husband.
The Great Wall was very, very far from her home.
Along the way, Lady Meng Jiang experienced countless bouts of wind, frost, rain, and snow.
She trekked through countless dangerous mountains and treacherous waters.
But Lady Meng Jiang didn’t once cry out in suffering, nor did she shed a single tear.
Finally, through her tenacious willpower and deep love for her husband, she arrived at the Great Wall.
At the time, the Great Wall had already become a very long city wall made up of individual construction sites.
Lady Meng Jiang searched each construction site, but didn’t find any trace of her husband.
She summoned the courage to ask a group of workers who were just starting work:
“Is there a person called Fan Xiliang around here?”
The workers said: “There is such a person, he’s new and came not too long ago.”
As soon as Lady Meng Jiang heard this, she was indescribably happy.
She continued to ask: “Then where is he?”
The workers looked at each other, and after a long time finally said:
“Fan Xiliang … died last month due to exhaustion and starvation.”
Lady Meng Jiang once again asked: “Then where is his body?”
The workers shook their heads and said:
“Alas, too many people have died, we are unable to bury them. Those above told us to fill him into the Great Wall.
Suddenly hearing this grievous news was a bolt from the blue for Lady Meng Jiang. She beat the Great Wall and began to cry loudly.
She cried for three full days and three nights. She cried until it was dark all around. Even the heavens and earth were moved.
Suddenly, amidst the sound of her weeping, there was a big crashing sound.
One large section of the Great Wall actually collapsed as if rocked by a major disaster. Piles of human bones were exposed.
But there were so many bones of the dead, which ones belonged to her husband?
Very quickly she recognized her husband’s corpse from the clothing she had made for him with her own hands.
Lady Meng Jiang guarded her husband’s corpose, and cried as though she was hovering between life and death.
Just as she was crying, Qin Shihuang led a large squadron of men and horses to pass through the area.
He had heard that Lady Meng Jiang collapsed the Great Wall with her crying, and got really angry.
He led the large squadron of men and horses to the bottom of the mountain, preparing to punish Lady Meng Jiang.
However, when he saw what a young and beautiful girl Lady Meng Jiang was, he immediately changed his mind, and had the idea to capture her.
Qin Shihuang wanted to take Lady Meng Jiang to be his wife. Lady Meng Jiang said:
“If you agree to three conditions, I will marry you.”
Qin Shihuang was very happy, and said beamingly:
“Don’t mention three conditions, even if you ask for thirty conditions, I will do as you say. Speak, what do you want?”
Lady Meng Jiang said:
“The first condition is, I want you to erect a headstone and decorate a tomb for my husband.
The second condition is, I want you to dress in mourning clothes for my husband.
The third condition is, I want you to accompany me to visit the ocean for three days.”
Qin Shihuang agreed.
After the second condition was met, Lady Meng Jiang said: “Let’s go! Let’s go to the ocean!”
Qin Shihuang was pleased beyond his expectations, thinking that after going to the ocean he could get married to Lady Meng Jiang.
Who would’ve known that just as he was feeling overjoyed, he would hear a “plop” sound.
Lady Meng Jiang had jumped into the ocean, and was never to be found again.
The story of Lady Meng Jiang collapsing the Great Wall with her crying has spread far and wide in China.
We can say that it is known by everyone. It is one of China’s Four Great Folktales.
In order to commemorate her, later generations decorated a grave and built a temple for her atop a mountain near the Shanhai Pass.
They named it the “Meng Jiangnu Temple”.
